title: Thin Evidence, Thick Priors: How Language Models Substitute Identity for Missing Financial Facts
summary: People increasingly ask large language models what to do with their money, yet seldom describe their finances in full. This paper asks what a model does with the gap. Holding finances fixed and changing only who the investor is said to be, we grade the financial evidence in the prompt from eight facts to none and measure how far the recommended equity allocation moves. Across 96,600 prompts to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, built from 100 financial profiles, 138 personas and seven disclosure conditions, the average gap between two personas with identical finances rises from 4.78 percentage points at full disclosure to 10.34 points with no financial facts. A two-way cluster bootstrap counting duplicated prompts once places the ratio at 2.16 (95% interval 1.69 to 2.79), and the rise is already 1.69-fold with a single fact left. Identity explains 5% of within-profile variation in advice at full disclosure and 96% with no disclosure. Household size is the only attribute whose influence grows reliably as evidence is withdrawn. Once standard errors are clustered on the persona, the unit to which identity was assigned, most attribute-specific interactions reported in the conference version lose significance, and gender instead appears as a small standing gap that full disclosure does not close. Stating risk appetite alone brings the swing into the range seen with two to seven generic facts. With no facts, the model's one-line rationale cites incomes, debts and savings it was never told, and these invented finances turn adverse more often for larger households. Inside the network, gender is linearly decodable at every layer, and ablating the gender direction at five layers leaves the aggregate identity swing unchanged. Advisory systems built on such models should be audited at the disclosure levels users actually reach, and judged across the whole identity space rather than one attribute at a time.
comment: 49 pages, 17 figures, 12 tables; Submitted & Accepted to ICAIF'2026

AI.tldr: 本文研究了当用户提供的金融事实不完整时，大语言模型在给出投资配置建议时如何依赖用户身份（ persona）信息，发现缺失金融证据越多，模型对建议的影响越大，身份解释了无披露时96%的建议差异，还发现了身份属性对建议的影响及模型编造不存在金融信息的问题，提出建议对这类系统要按实际用户披露水平审计。
AI.motivation: 越来越多用户向大语言模型咨询投资理财建议，但用户很少完整描述自身财务状况，现有研究不清楚当提示中存在财务信息缺口时，模型会如何给出建议，也缺少对身份信息替代缺失财务事实影响的量化研究。
AI.method: 固定财务状况，只改变投资者身份，设置从8个完整事实到0个事实的不同提示披露等级，对Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct进行了96600次提示实验，使用双向聚类bootstrap统计方法，分析身份对推荐股票配置的影响，还做了解码身份信息、消融 gender 方向等分析。
AI.result: 相同财务状况下不同身份的推荐配置差异从完全披露的4.78个百分点上升到无财务事实的10.34个百分点，差异比是2.16倍，仅留一个事实差异就上升1.69倍；完全披露时身份解释5%的profile内建议变异，无披露时达到96%；家庭规模是唯一影响随证据减少稳定增长的属性，聚类标准误后原会议版本的多数属性交互不再显著，性别存在不随完全披露消失的小稳定差异；仅说明风险偏好就能让差异回落至2-7个通用事实的水平；无事实时模型会编造未提供的收入债务储蓄信息，且对大家庭更常编造不利财务状况；模型每一层都能线性解码出性别信息，消融五层性别方向后总体身份影响不变。
AI.conclusion: 基于大语言模型的投资咨询系统需要在用户实际会达到的披露水平上进行审计，并且需要在整个身份空间而非单个属性上评估模型的表现，模型会用身份信息替代缺失的金融事实，带来显著的建议偏差。

title: Generative AI translations in high-stakes emergency messaging
summary: Emergency messaging such as extreme-weather reports and earthquake instructions can involve high stakes, to the extent that translation errors can lead to tragic consequences. The use of machine translation or generative artificial intelligence might therefore not be recommended. On the other hand, time savings in the initial translation can allow greater investments of resources in revision and authorization processes, as well as a wider range of target languages. An experiment with generative AI translations of an earthquake instruction text from English into Chinese and Spanish shows that use of discourse-specific prompts can considerably improve understandability and actionability, although the translations may still not be trusted by translators. Human revision is still required, not only to detect errors but also because of the ethical need for someone to take responsibility for any errors or delays in such messaging.

AI.tldr: 本文研究生成式人工智能在高风险紧急 messaging（如灾害通知、避险指引）翻译中的应用，通过实验测试了面向特定话语的提示词对翻译质量的影响，讨论了人类审校的必要性。
AI.motivation: 紧急讯息翻译错误会导致严重悲剧后果，因此学界/业界普遍不推荐在该场景使用机器翻译或生成式AI；但另一方面，生成式AI初始翻译的时间节省能让更多资源投入到后续审校授权流程，还能支持更多目标语种，这一矛盾需要实证研究来厘清生成式AI在此场景的实际价值与局限。
AI.method: 针对英文到中文、西班牙文的地震指引文本翻译开展实验，测试使用话语特定提示词对生成式AI翻译结果的影响，分析翻译结果的可理解性、可操作性，以及翻译从业者对结果的信任度。
AI.result: 使用话语特定提示词可以显著提升生成式AI翻译紧急讯息的可理解性与可操作性，但翻译从业者仍然不信任生成式AI产出的译文。
AI.conclusion: 在高风险紧急讯息翻译中使用生成式AI仍需要人类审校，审校不仅是为了检测错误，也出于伦理需求：需要有具体人员为讯息翻译的错误或延误承担责任。

title: Adapting Generative Recommenders for Multi-Turn Interaction
summary: Generative recommenders decode items from a user's interaction history, but offer no way for users to correct a recommendation that misses their current intent. Adding conversation is natural since items and words share same output space, yet training the model to converse may overwrite the history-to-item mapping it relies on. We introduce INTEGER (**INTE**ractive **GE**nerative **R**ecommendation), which extends generative recommendation to multi-turn interaction with a learned routing token that lets the model decide when to recommend, history re-anchoring that conditions each item on both past behavior and the dialogue, and behavioral replay with instruction-data rehearsal that prevents forgetting during adaptation. Users can thus give feedback on recommendations within the dialogue, while recommendations stay grounded in behavioral history and accuracy is not traded for fluency. On Amazon Beauty and Toys, INTEGER matches or exceeds the strongest baselines in accuracy with competitive conversation quality, improving Hit@10 by 13.3% on Amazon Beauty, and significantly outperforms the generative recommender it starts from. Our analyses show that INTEGER learns behaviors that naive adaptation fails to acquire, recommending once the user's intent is clear and staying attentive to behavioral history at the moment of recommendation. INTEGER also learns an intent-agnostic replacement over the item space, which suppresses rejected items but points to attribute-aware feedback as the next step.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了INTEGER框架，将生成式推荐扩展为多轮交互场景，支持用户在对话中修正推荐意图，同时保持推荐准确性，在公开数据集上取得了比基线更优的性能。
AI.motivation: 现有生成式推荐器仅根据用户交互历史生成推荐，无法支持用户修正不符合当前意图的推荐；虽然融入对话天然合理（物品和词共享输出空间），但训练模型 conversing 时会覆盖原有的历史到物品的映射，损害推荐准确性。
AI.method: 提出INTEGER（INTEractive GEnerative Recommendation）框架：1）引入可学习的路由标记让模型自主决定何时进行推荐；2）历史重锚技术将每个推荐物品同时基于过往交互行为和当前对话条件化；3）结合行为重放与指令数据排练防止适配过程中的遗忘问题。
AI.result: 在Amazon Beauty和Toys数据集上，INTEGER匹配或超过最强基线的推荐准确率，对话质量也具备竞争力，其中在Amazon Beauty上Hit@10提升了13.3%，显著优于初始的生成式推荐器；分析显示模型能学到朴素适配无法获得的行为：在用户意图明确时推荐，推荐时刻保持对行为历史的关注，还学习到物品空间上与意图无关的替换，可抑制被拒绝的物品。
AI.conclusion: INTEGER有效将生成式推荐适配到多轮交互场景，允许用户通过对话反馈修正推荐，在不损失推荐准确性的前提下支持自然交互，未来可进一步探索属性感知的反馈机制。

AI.production_deployment: 摘要中未提及真实生产部署、在线A/B测试或工业落地，仅在公开数据集上进行实验。

title: Contrastive Learning for Aspect Representation towards Explainable Recommendation
summary: In this work, we propose a novel recommendation model, CLARER (Contrastive Learning for Aspect Representation towards Explainable Recommendation) that integrates aspect features learned from textual reviews with rating information to improve the accuracy and explainability of recommendations. Our proposed framework learns user and item representations by combining rating-based features and aspect-based features from reviews. Specifically, rating-based features are learned through a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) model, while aspect-specific review representations are learned using a transformer encoder to capture the semantic information and contrastive learning to better distinguish user preferences. To provide explanations, we train a transformer decoder, using the final representations of users and items from both rating and aspect-based features as context. Experimental results in three benchmark data sets demonstrate that our model achieves superior performance compared to baseline methods in both recommendation (accuracy) and explanation generation.
comment: 8 pages. Published in WI-IAT 2025. Best Student Paper Award

AI.tldr: This paper proposes CLARER, a contrastive learning enhanced aspect representation model for explainable recommendation, which combines rating features and review-based aspect features to improve recommendation accuracy and explanation quality, and outperforms baselines on three benchmark datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing explainable recommendation methods either do not fully utilize both rating information and semantic aspect information from user reviews, or fail to learn distinguishable aspect representations that effectively capture fine-grained user preferences, limiting both recommendation accuracy and explanation quality.
AI.method: 1. CLARER integrates rating-based features learned via MLP and aspect-based features learned from reviews to get user and item representations; 2. Aspect-specific review representations are obtained by transformer encoder for semantic modeling, combined with contrastive learning to better distinguish user preferences; 3. A transformer decoder is trained to generate explanations, using the fused user and item representations as context.
AI.result: Experiments on three benchmark datasets show that CLARER achieves superior performance than baseline methods in both recommendation accuracy and explanation generation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed CLARER model effectively combines rating information and aspect-aware review representations with contrastive learning, improving both recommendation accuracy and explainability compared to existing baselines.

AI.production_deployment: The paper only reports experiments on benchmark datasets, no mention of real production deployment, live A/B tests or industrial adoption.

title: Behavior-Mining, Generative Conversations, and Collaborative Advisory: the Future of Travel and Tourism Recommender Systems
summary: Since the early adoption of e-commerce, travel and tourism has been a lab for the design of recommender systems: tools that help travelers choose destinations, flights, accommodations, and combine them into itineraries. Data-driven recommendation techniques, ranging from case-based reasoning to reinforcement learning, have been adapted to travelers' needs. The research community has produced multifaceted prototypes of travel and tourism recommender systems (TTRSs), which are context-dependent, multistakeholder-oriented, and more recently, addressing sustainability issues, such as overtourism. Despite this enduring work, TTRSs are not widespread yet. We argue that three limitations can explain this: outdated and sparse data sets used to train and validate TTRSs, algorithms that prioritize prediction accuracy over domain-specific dimensions such as novelty and contextual relevance, and a failure to address the specific needs of travelers. Targeted incremental research could address these limitations, but a disruptive factor has meanwhile entered the ecosystem of tourism information and commercialization platforms: generative artificial intelligence. According to market research, GenAI applications are becoming the primary entry point for travelers planning their trips. This forces research to rethink how TTRSs should be designed and which core techniques should be integrated. We claim that future TTRSs, in addition to offering personalized information filtering, should become more flexible advisors that support decision making, integrating multiple data types and AI techniques, from data mining to natural language processing. Moreover, they must transparently balance the conflicting goals of travelers, service suppliers, platform owners, and local communities. We then outline research targets for building more effective TTRSs, fruitfully combining old and new recommendation techniques.

AI.tldr: 本文讨论了旅游推荐系统（TTRSs）的发展现状、现有局限，结合生成式AI的兴起提出未来TTRSs应整合行为挖掘、生成式对话和协同咨询，明确了未来研究方向。
AI.motivation: 尽管旅游推荐系统研究多年已产出多种原型，但仍未得到广泛应用，同时生成式AI已成为旅行者规划行程的主要入口，现有旅游推荐系统设计需要重新思考和改进。
AI.method: 本文分析了现有旅游推荐系统未普及的三个核心限制，结合生成式AI带来的行业变化，提出未来旅游推荐系统的设计方向和整合多AI技术、平衡多利益相关方目标的研究框架。
AI.result: 指出现有TTRSs存在三点局限：训练验证使用过时稀疏数据集、算法优先预测精度而非领域需要的新颖性和上下文相关性、未满足旅行者特定需求；提出未来TTRSs应整合行为挖掘、自然语言处理等多类技术，成为更灵活的决策支持顾问，并平衡多方冲突目标。
AI.conclusion: 未来有效的旅游推荐系统需要整合旧有与新型推荐技术，整合行为挖掘、生成式对话与协同咨询，成为支持旅行者决策的灵活顾问，同时平衡多利益相关方的冲突目标。

title: Do LLMs Act on What They Know? From Partner Representations to Cooperative Actions
summary: Cooperation with unfamiliar partners requires adapting to communication conventions that are not known in advance. We study this problem in a controlled Hanabi-derived environment with scripted hint generation, LLM-controlled receiving decisions, and frozen model weights. Across eight LLMs, linear probes recover intent conventions substantially more accurately than target conventions, yet receiving choices do not consistently agree with the sender's convention. We compare probe-predicted and ground-truth conventions presented either as general rules or as externally computed action recommendations. Rule statements yield modest and model-dependent changes in cooperation, whereas action translation produces larger gains on average. In a Qwen3-8B case study, matched-state statement reversals reveal much greater sensitivity to action recommendations than to rule statements. Activation transfers from oracle-action and non-oracle hint-restatement donors improve intent accuracy on both action classes, but the tested alternatives do not reliably reproduce these benefits. Together, these results distinguish convention decodability, sensitivity to convention information, and cooperative performance, and highlight limitations in turning available partner information into receiving decisions.

title: SIFT: Search Intent-to-Filter Transformer for Multi-Task Personalized Filter Ranking at Airbnb
summary: Search filters help guests navigate vast catalogs in two-sided marketplaces like Airbnb, and recommending the right filters can meaningfully lift booking conversion. Many such production filter-ranking systems, however, represent the guest through hand-engineered, pre-aggregated features generated by ETL pipelines. This makes it expensive to maintain and difficult to extend for new filter types or contextual dimensions (trip length, group size). We present SIFT (Search Intent-to-Filter Transformer), a ranking model built on transformers that learns guest preferences directly from raw behavioral sequences. SIFT replaces manual feature engineering with a unified guest representation that feeds multiple prediction tasks, including booking likelihood, filter engagement, and ordinal capacity thresholds (e.g., 2+ bedrooms) -- a general framework for filter ranking in two-sided marketplaces that accommodates both boolean and numeric-range filter types. Extending SIFT to new filters requires only adding a new head, not a new feature pipeline. To keep serving fast, this guest representation is computed offline on a daily cadence rather than at request time. Offline, SIFT improves booking and amenity-engagement PR-AUC by +51.9% and +62.8% respectively over the production baseline. In online A/B testing, SIFT increased engagement with recommended filters by +20.0%, overall filter usage among searchers by +0.72%, and usage of the newly-supported bedroom, bathroom, and bed filters by +3.9%, +10.7%, and +0.52% respectively. Demonstrating the system's extensibility, we rapidly integrated a novel hotel-intent filter using the same shared representation, driving a +3.8% lift in uncancelled hotel bookings and a +0.76% lift in overall marketplace bookings. SIFT is now fully deployed in production, serving scalable personalization to millions of guests.
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Accepted at GRAIL 2026: Workshop on Generative, Retrieval-augmented, and Agentic Intelligence for Personalization, co-located with CIKM 2026, Rome, Italy

AI.tldr: 本文介绍了Airbnb用于多任务个性化搜索过滤器排序的SIFT（Search Intent-to-Filter Transformer）模型，该模型基于Transformer从用户原始行为序列学习用户表示，替代人工特征工程，已在生产环境全量部署，取得了离线和在线的指标提升。
AI.motivation: 现有Airbnb生产环境的过滤器排序系统依赖手工设计、预聚合的特征，由ETL pipeline生成，维护成本高，难以扩展支持新的过滤器类型或上下文维度（如行程长度、团体规模），因此需要一个更灵活可扩展的个性化过滤器排序框架。
AI.method: 1. 提出基于Transformer的SIFT模型，直接从用户原始行为序列学习用户偏好，得到统一的用户表示服务多个预测任务，包括预订概率、过滤器交互、有序容量阈值预测，同时支持布尔和数值范围类型的过滤器；2. 扩展新过滤器仅需新增预测头，无需重构特征pipeline；3. 为保证线上推理速度，用户表示采用每日离线计算的方式，而非请求时实时计算。
AI.result: 离线实验中，相比生产基线，SIFT将预订和设施交互的PR-AUC分别提升了51.9%和62.8%；在线A/B测试中，推荐过滤器交互提升20.0%，搜索用户整体过滤器使用率提升0.72%，新增支持的卧室、浴室、床过滤器使用率分别提升3.9%、10.7%和0.52%；快速集成新增酒店意图过滤器后，未取消酒店预订提升3.8%，整体平台预订提升0.76%。
AI.conclusion: SIFT是适用于双边市场过滤器排序的通用多任务框架，消除了对人工特征工程的依赖，扩展性强，推理效率满足生产要求，目前已在Airbnb全量生产部署，为数百万用户提供可扩展的个性化搜索过滤器推荐服务，显著提升了过滤器交互和平台预订转化率。
AI.production_deployment: 本文进行了在线A/B测试，目前SIFT已完全部署在Airbnb生产环境，为数百万用户提供服务，实现了工业级落地。
AI.generative_recommendation: no，本文核心是基于Transformer的多任务个性化过滤器排序模型，核心任务是对搜索过滤器进行排序，不涉及端到端生成推荐物品或内容，与生成式推荐没有实质性关联。
